content:
maria: Heads up — we started seeing intermittent DNS errors for internal service names in eu-west yesterday evening. Services hit sporadic 5xx when resolving svc.cluster.local and some internal-svc.company.local. Not every pod, seems bursty and correlated with deploys.

sam: Ugh. Symptoms? NXDOMAIN, SERVFAIL, or stale A records? Any pattern by node/az?

maria: Mostly SERVFAIL followed by a bunch of stale-looking A records returning old IPs for ~30s. Eventually resolves correctly. Happened in prod and staging but more frequent in prod-east->eu-west cross-region calls.

zach: Can you paste the node /etc/resolv.conf from an affected host and from a pod? We had issues before when kubelet used the stub resolver vs upstream file.

maria: Paste below (host vs pod):
```
# host /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options edns0 trust-ad
search eu-west.internal.company.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local 

# pod /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 10.244.0.10  # node-local-dns svc IP
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local eu-west.internal.company.local
options ndots:5
```

olivia: So host is using systemd-resolved stub (127.0.0.53) but pods talk to node-local-dns. If systemd-resolved is returning SERVFAIL intermittently it won't be visible to pod lookups unless the node-local-dns is forwarding to it. Does node-local-dns forward to 127.0.0.53?

maria: Yes — node-local-dns is configured to forward fallback queries to 127.0.0.53 and then to our VPC resolver. I pulled a packet capture on an affected node: we see repeated queries to 127.0.0.53 and then truncated responses with SERVFAIL until a background refresh.

sam: That smells like systemd-resolved caching behaviour + upstream EC2 resolver flapping. Also glibc resolver behavior matters: if /etc/resolv.conf is the stub file, glibc will make the app query the stub which does all real work. If kubelet passed the stub resolv.conf into pods earlier (some kubelet configs do), pods might get unexpected behavior. But your pod resolv.conf points to node-local-dns — so forward path is pod -> node-local-dns -> systemd-resolved -> VPC. Lots of caches and TTL mismatches.

zach: Two quick checks:
1) run `dig +short @127.0.0.53 some-service.svc.cluster.local A` and `dig +short @10.244.0.10 some-service.svc.cluster.local A` around the time of failure and compare TTLs.
2) check systemd-resolved logs: `journalctl -u systemd-resolved --since "10 minutes ago"` for SERVFAIL or upstream timeouts.

maria: Ran the digs. Snip: 
```
# to 127.0.0.53 -> SERVFAIL for ~20s then returns old IP with TTL 0
;; -> ;;; res_options: ndots:1
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.53#53(127.0.0.53)
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345

# to 10.244.0.10 -> forwards -> sometimes returns cached A (old ip) TTL=0 until node-local-dns refreshes upstream
```

olivia: TTL=0 on cached A is bad — indicates a stale cache entry. node-local-dns should respect TTLs from upstream and not serve expired entries. Might be a bug in the caching layer where expired entries are returned during upstream outage. Which node-local-dns image/tag?

maria: node-local-dns: v0.8.0 (our custom build with a small forwarder tweak). We recently rolled that in last week.

sam: OK — hypothesis: our custom node-local-dns change + systemd-resolved stub forwarding created a race where upstream transient failures cause node-local-dns to return expired entries (TTL 0) instead of NXDOMAIN or failing fast. That would explain the 5xx burst pattern during upstream hiccups.

zach: Recommended mitigation path:
- roll back node-local-dns to previous stable tag on a small canary subset of nodes (2 nodes)
- change kubelet --resolv-conf flags on a canary pool so pods don't receive the systemd stub file directly (point to /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf non-stub)
- add a short-term rule in node-local-dns to drop entries with TTL<=0 instead of serving them

maria: I'll open a quick patch: rollback daemonset to v0.7.2 on canary nodes and monitor. patch command I'm going to run:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system set image daemonset/node-local-dns node-local-dns=registry.redwood/node-local-dns:v0.7.2 --record
```
We'll also scale the daemonset replica count down/up for canary nodes only.

olivia: Also add alert to dns-monitor that flags replies with TTL<=0 being served. dns-monitor-bot can create an incident if rate > 5/min.

dns-monitor-bot: alert: dns_ttl_zero_count exceeded threshold in eu-west (rate 12/min) — creating incident INC-2026-443

sam: If rollback stabilizes, we should plan a proper fix: either stop forwarding to systemd-resolved stub (use direct VPC resolver from node-local-dns) or upgrade our node-local-dns to respect expired entries and do failover behavior. Longer term: standardize resolv.conf path used by kubelet across all clusters to avoid split-horizon surprises.

maria: Agreed. For immediate steps: I started the rollback on canary nodes (2/2 updated), monitoring logs. If those nodes look healthy for 10m we'll continue to a 10% roll then full. I'll post updates here.

zach: Thanks. If it still flaps after rollback, we should toggle node-local-dns fallback upstream to the VPC resolver before systemd-resolved so we bypass the stub. But try rollback first.

maria: Update: canary nodes stable for 12 minutes, no SERVFAIL spikes, dns-monitor-bot alert rate back to baseline. Proceeding to 10% now. Will post final when full roll complete.

olivia: Nice work. Remember to file a postmortem and include timeline + packet captures + the kubelet resolv.conf behavior so we don't hit this again.

maria: Will do. Filing a short postmortem and tagging eng-infra + eng-runtime.
